description: main declares 'int *values;' (pointers are not in the subset) and then uses 'values' five times.
injected_faults: line 6: pointer declaration 'int *values;' is not supported
notes: Expected under plan 004: raw 6. SYN-UNSUPPORTED-FEATURE 6 (caused_by: none), SEM-UNDECLARED-VAR 7 (caused_by: R5), SEM-UNDECLARED-VAR 8 (caused_by: R5), SEM-UNDECLARED-VAR 9 (caused_by: R5), SEM-UNDECLARED-VAR 11 (caused_by: R5), SEM-UNDECLARED-VAR 13 (caused_by: R5). Panic skips '* values' and consumes the ';'. The IDENT 'values' was never consumed, but because the error is SYN-UNSUPPORTED-FEATURE the section 5 declarator-name rule gives declared_names [(values, <unsupported>)] (it follows '*' and precedes ';'), so R5 links the five uses to the syntax record. gcc accepts the file, so gcc_rejects is false.
